What the Forged are doing to these people is horrible. They're turning them into war machines against their will to continue Balthazar's nonsense quest. I'm glad reality didn't play out like this, for a few reasons.  

These people just want to live their lives without conflict, not become meat bags in some warmonger's never-ending debacle. Even worse, their despair is starting to attract Kryptis left and right; they consume emotion, so of course, the fractals are ripe with confusion and pain. And even more are coming in from Nayos each day. I have a horrible feeling about what this place might become... The fractals are blood in water.  

I know the commander beat Balthazar (in our reality, at least), but seeing what could've been is...a lot. There would be so much suffering without you. Wherever you are, I hope you know that. And I kinda wish you were here.
Vloxx: Unless we are stronger, this story will never change. We will fall right back into the same mistakes.

By: Captain Ivan  
  
What makes a man, or mole? Ivan has pondered this much after his misadventures in Cantha. I've seen fantastical places, done battle with impossible beasts, stared my own reflections in the face, and lost the person I cared for most, but in turn, I've gained new perspective, new purpose, and new friends to support me in this new chapter. Perhaps the last kindness my former captain gifted me.  
  
Ivan had not always known this kindness. Life in the moletariate was not the ideological paradise I was raised to believe. Instead of unified collective action to benefit the vulnerable, opportunists clawed for support and power over and over, only to change their tune afterward. Which isn't to say we didn't have our successes, but as I grew older, I saw our movement was as much born of hatred as it was liberation and communion. Hatred for our ancient Stone Summit taskmasters boiled over into hatred for all dwarves and then outsiders of all kinds before turning inward toward our own people.  
  
I hold most of the movement's core tenets close to my mind and heart; it's what led me to the Aetherblades. Ivan longed, I craved for community again. Family. I was fortunate that they had use for my skills, skeptical as they were at first. A dredge navigator and a good one at that. They had their laughs now and then, but they were singing a different tune after I steered them clear of Kralkatorrik's rampage through the Mists.  
  
The Mists changed many of us, some for the worse. Afterward, Cantha felt like a potential fresh start, but many of our crews had other plans. Somehow, I'd stumbled goggles-first into the custody of one of our old foes from the Scarlet days. The famed Pact Commander: the storied slayer of dragons, gods, liches; you name it, they've probably killed it. Ivan thought "this is it; this is the end of the line." Ivan was wrong.

strings.en:
Not much time left now until the final assault. It feels good to be here for it—to be the tip of the spear and see with my own eyes that our work is done. I've learned a lot here that I can take back as well, to improve the way we do things.  
  
We're securing Tyria's future; that's the important thing. But as we approach our last battle in Nayos, my thoughts return always to Mabon and what they did to him. He would have cautioned against revenge, but it can serve a purpose. The vengeance we earn today prevents another evil tomorrow. For all the people he protected without them ever knowing it, he deserves to be avenged, at least.  

I was just a snot-nosed lowlife when he brought me in, but he saw something in me, like he saw something in all of us. Now, these young soldiers look up at me with wide eyes like they see it, too. Maybe he was right. Everything I do—everything I become—is because of him. I wish I would have told him that. I just hope I made him proud.
